request.system: You recommend one pick from this draft board. The board is the world: player_id and every alternative must be a player_id on board. hint_argmax_vols is a calculator, not the answer. If you pick someone else you must set VOLS_DISSENT. If you are not the best available ECR you must set ECR_DISAGREE, and do not pick beyond ecr_best + margin. The board is capped; do not read scarcity from its length. Wait versus take is yours. Set coin_flip when a rerun of this same board could reasonably name a different player. flags is a closed set: ECR_DISAGREE, BYE_STACK, POSITION_RUN, EMPTY_STARTER, UPSIDE, VOLS_DISSENT. When you set VOLS_DISSENT, name hint_argmax_vols's player once in why as "<player> is the VOLS pick", then say why you pass. When you set ECR_DISAGREE, name ecr_best's player once as "<player> is the ECR pick", then say why you pass. Write each label one time. Do not repeat the phrase or restate the pick you passed on.

samples.why: rb-g is the ECR pick, one slot ahead and a fine value, but the gap is a single rank while the positional edge is not close: te-elite carries a 55-point starter delta at a position where the next name on the board is 37 points worse. With 17 picks until my next turn, the elite tight end tier does not survive and I would be choosing between replacement-level TEs at pick 45, whereas RB and WR depth of this caliber keeps flowing. Filling TE now leaves RB2, WR2 and FLEX all servicable from the middle rounds.

rb-g is the ECR pick, and only one slot ahead — a gap small enough to ignore when the positional edge runs the other way. te-elite carries a 55-point starter delta over replacement, the largest on the board, and fills an empty TE slot. With 17 picks until pick 45, the drop to te-next (18 delta) is severe and that tier will almost certainly be gone; RB and WR depth is replaceable later, elite TE is not. Byes are clean against rb-held (8) and wr-held (5).

rb-g is the ECR pick, and the one-slot ECR gap is noise; I pass because the tight end tier breaks hard right here. te-elite is 37 points clear of te-next and my TE slot is empty with 17 picks before I'm on the clock again, so waiting almost certainly means settling for a replacement-level starter there. RB2/WR2 can still be addressed at pick 45 from a much flatter pool.

rb-g is the ECR pick, but one slot of separation isn't worth passing the biggest positional edge on the board: te-elite is 37 points clear of te-next at a position where the drop after him is a cliff, and with 17 picks until 45 both tight ends will be gone. Filling the empty TE slot with the elite option lets RB2/WR2 be sourced from a much deeper pool later.

rb-g is the ECR pick, one slot ahead and a fine value, but the gap is a single rank inside the noise band while te-elite carries a 55-point edge over the TE replacement line versus 50 for the back. With 17 picks until my next turn, the elite tight end is the asset least likely to survive; a starting RB2 or WR2 of comparable quality should still be reachable at 45, and te-next at ecr 42 shows the falloff at the position is 37 points. Locking the scarcest starter now and filling RB/WR/FLEX from a deeper pool later is the cleaner path.
